inputs.sbc_source: J-GAAP filer; no share-based payment add-back in the FY2026 (YE Mar-2026) consolidated cash flow statement and no stock-option/restricted-stock line in the tanshin (grep of 1808.T_Annual_FY2026.txt returns nothing). Director restricted-stock grants are immaterial. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 purchase of treasury shares JPY20.1bn (1808.T_Annual_FY2026.txt:913); FY2025 JPY0.5bn. Count held flat; buybacks are a shareholder return, not a dilution offset, in an SBC-zero name.
inputs.fy0_note: CSV period label FY2026 = fiscal year ended 2026-03-31 (the company calls this 'FY2025'). Forecast year 1 = FY2027 in CSV labelling = year ending 2027-03-31, the year management has guided.
inputs.balance_sheet_note: Q1 FY2027 (June 2026) balance sheet: interest-bearing debt JPY418.5bn, cash JPY227.6bn, net debt JPY190.9bn. June is the seasonal cash low (March 2026: cash 288.1bn, debt 425.0bn, net debt 136.9bn) because real estate inventory and construction receivables build through the year; the latest filing is used as instructed, which is the more conservative anchor.
inputs.share_count_basis: 264.856m shares outstanding net of treasury at 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin; weighted average for the quarter 264.8m). No convertibles or material options; treated as fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is zero so there is nothing to expense, and buybacks are treated as return of capital rather than modelled as a falling count.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. Risk-free 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct-2026, post BoJ normalisation); Japan ERP 6.0%; equity beta 1.15 for a leveraged condominium contractor/developer -> cost of equity ~8.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~1.2% (FY2026 interest expense ~JPY5bn on JPY420bn of borrowings), ~0.85% after 31% tax. Market-value weights E 63% / D 37% (market cap ~JPY716bn vs debt JPY418.5bn) -> 5.7%, rounded up to 6.0% to allow for further JGB yield normalisation. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, the JFTC investigation and overseas execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: J-GAAP filer: operating leases are expensed inside operating profit/EBITDA; finance leases are immaterial. No lease principal is deducted from the flows and no lease liabilities are added to net debt (total_debt is interest-bearing borrowings and bonds only). One treatment, consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests JPY0.7bn at Mar-2026 (first appearance, FY2026 tanshin:876) and NCI profit JPY0.1bn - immaterial, no deduction and no leakage adjustment; flows are treated as 100% attributable.
inputs.working_capital_note: Haseko is a developer as well as a contractor: real estate inventory (JPY586.7bn at Mar-2026) and 'real estate and overseas investment' (JPY819.7bn) are funded by borrowings, so reported FCF is lumpy and structurally below net income (10-year FY2017-FY2026 cumulative FCF JPY239.6bn vs net income JPY585.8bn; NI+D&A-capex JPY378bn, so inventory/working-capital absorbed ~JPY138bn against JPY486bn of revenue growth, i.e. ~28% of each yen of revenue growth). The engine's wc_capture is therefore NEGATIVE: base -25% of the revenue change (credit for the Evolution Plan asset-turnover initiatives), bear -35% (decade actual plus land-bank write-downs), bull -15%. In a revenue decline the sign releases cash, which is what inventory liquidation does.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (engine), with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (JPY WACC, J-GAAP leases expensed, SBC-zero, negative working-capital capture, cross-shareholdings in the bridge). Routing: Haseko is an operating company - 49% of sales and most of profit are condominium construction contracts, 8% recurring management/leasing, 40% for-sale real estate. It straddles the 'inventory-heavy developer' row, but the profit engine is a contracting business with a 10-year average EBITDA margin of ~10% and positive cumulative FCF, not a land subdivider with structurally negative FCF, so the whole group is valued on one owner-FCF model and the development inventory build is charged explicitly through a negative working-capital capture rather than by switching to a blended NTA/P-E method. Peak-earnings check: the FY2026 EBITDA margin of 8.4% (FY2027 guidance 8.7%) is BELOW the FY2017-FY2026 average of ~10% and well below the FY2018-19 peak of 12-13%, so the base case is mid-cycle to below-mid-cycle on margin; revenue, however, is at a record (backlog JPY940bn) so growth is faded to 1% within six years. last_fcf is the FY2026 reported FCF of JPY136.3bn, which is a working-capital-release high (3-year average JPY70.1bn); the component build does not carry it forward. Fresh build - no prior DCF, no memory entry.

equity_bridge.item: Listed investment securities (cross-shareholdings) at fair value, net of 30% tax on the unrealised gain
equity_bridge.note: Investment securities JPY146.3bn at Mar-2026 (1808.T_Annual_FY2026.txt:870) less JPY88.3bn classified by the company as real-estate/overseas investments (:1008), which are operating assets whose returns sit inside segment profit. The ~JPY58bn remainder is available-for-sale equities (valuation difference JPY20.8bn after tax, :873), whose dividend income is non-operating and therefore excluded from the EBITDA-based flows - matching-asset rule. Unrealised gain ~JPY30bn pre-tax taxed at 30% -> JPY49bn added.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 7.4% vs EPS 5-yr CAGR 3.9% (>30% divergence) and revenue 9.5%: EPS is depressed by FY2025 impairments (JPY16.9bn extraordinary losses, EPS 126) and FY2026 extraordinary losses (JPY4.6bn); FY2027 guided EPS of JPY249 would restore a ~8% 5-yr EPS CAGR. Growth is faded from guidance (8.4%) to 1% rather than compounding the 7.4% equity CAGR, because revenue and backlog are at records.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF (SBC 0, interest income not stripped - the company is a net borrower). FCF CAGRs are undefined: FY2023 FCF was -JPY87.3bn and FY2021 JPY2.1bn (negative or near-zero bases). Use levels instead: 3-yr average owner FCF FY2024-26 JPY70.1bn vs FY2021-23 average -JPY15.5bn; 10-yr cumulative JPY239.6bn (~41% of cumulative net income) because development inventory absorbs cash. Period labels: CSV FY2026 = year ended 2026-03-31.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 8.4% = FY2027 sales guidance JPY1,380bn (Q1 22.6% of plan, on track). Y2 5% from the book-to-bill: FY2026 orders JPY726.7bn vs completed-construction revenue JPY625.2bn, backlog guided to JPY940bn at Mar-2027. Thereafter faded to 1% by Y9 for Tokyo new-condo supply at a 50-year low, an affordability ceiling after +21.8% price inflation in 2025, and demographics.
base.margin_rationale: FY2027 guidance OP JPY110bn + D&A ~JPY9.5bn = 8.7% EBITDA margin (construction GP ratio 15.9%, Q1 running 17.7%). Ramps to 9.0% - still one point below the FY2017-FY2026 average of ~10% and three to four points below the FY2018-19 peak - to allow for ~5%/yr construction cost inflation only partly passed through.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 capex JPY21.1bn = 1.66% of sales; decade average ~2.1% (PCa plant, income property). 1.8% holds a modest investment programme.
base.tax_rationale: Japan statutory effective ~30.6%; FY2026 current tax JPY36.4bn on pre-tax JPY89.5bn was inflated by non-deductible impairments. 31% cash rate throughout.

bull.narrative: Construction GP ratio holds the Q1 FY2027 level of ~17% rather than the 15.9% guided, data-centre and rental/company-housing orders keep intake above JPY700bn, EBITDA margin returns to the decade average of ~10.5% (vs 12-13% at the FY2018-19 peak), the Evolution Plan's asset-turnover targets lift FCF conversion (wc capture -15%), the light-asset US model turns overseas to profit from FY2028, and ROE reaches the 13% FY2030 target.

bear.narrative: The backlog carries FY2027 but BoJ rate normalisation plus record condo prices hit affordability: private-sector condo orders fall, FY2028-29 revenue contracts, construction cost inflation (~5%/yr) is not passed through and the EBITDA margin drops to 6% (FY2013-14 levels were ~5%). Land-bank and Hawaii impairments recur, the JFTC bid-rigging case against Haseko Reform ends in a surcharge and lost large-scale repair orders, and inventory turnover stays at the decade's -35% capture. Margin recovers only to 7.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands on guidance (sales JPY1,380bn, OP JPY110bn, net profit JPY66bn) off a record JPY940bn backlog; growth fades from 8% to 1% as Tokyo new-condo supply stays at multi-decade lows and demographics bite, while the recurring management/leasing book (453k units) and rental-housing/non-residential orders cushion the construction cycle. EBITDA margin settles at 9%, below the 10-year average, and development inventory keeps absorbing a quarter of every yen of revenue growth, so FCF conversion stays well under 100% of net income. Overseas losses narrow but the US pivot is not a profit driver.
scenario_narratives.bull: Construction GP ratio holds the Q1 FY2027 ~17% level, orders stay above JPY700bn on data-centre and rental housing work, EBITDA margin recovers to the decade average of ~10.5%, asset turnover improves FCF conversion, and ROE reaches the 13% Evolution Plan target - with growth fading to 1.5% rather than 1%.
scenario_narratives.bear: A rate-driven affordability shock cuts private-sector condo orders after the backlog runs off: revenue contracts ~10% over FY2028-30, margins fall to 6% as cost inflation is absorbed, impairments and a JFTC surcharge recur, and inventory liquidation funds the dividend. Recovery to 7.5% margins and 1% growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a single-country, single-product business leveraged to the Tokyo/Kansai condominium cycle at record prices and a 50-year supply low, with JPY418bn of debt funding an JPY820bn inventory/land bank into a BoJ tightening cycle, plus a live two-region JFTC bid-rigging investigation of a subsidiary. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: the bull case needs cost inflation to be fully passed through AND condo demand to hold AND overseas to turn - three independent things. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF of a cyclical Japanese contractor-developer, discounted in JPY at 6% with risk carried in the scenario flows and a 25/50/25 weighting. The decisive judgments are (1) the EBITDA margin is held at 9% in the base case, a point below the decade average and well under the FY2018-19 peak, so the model is not capitalising a peak; (2) development inventory is charged as a negative working-capital capture on revenue growth (-25% base), which is why owner FCF runs at roughly 40-60% of net income rather than the FY2026 release-driven JPY136bn; (3) terminal value is capped at 12-15x owner FCF (Gordon at 6%/1% would be ~20x) because a developer with a debt-funded land bank should not be capitalised as a mature compounder; (4) cross-shareholdings whose dividends are excluded from the flows are added back in the bridge at tax-effected fair value.
key_risks_to_valuation: Working-capital capture: every 10pp on wc_capture is worth roughly JPY10bn/yr of FCF in the growth years; the historical -28% could prove too harsh if the Evolution Plan turnover targets are met, or too lenient in a land-price correction
Margin: the base 9% EBITDA margin is below the decade average; a return to 12% (FY2018) would add ~JPY40bn/yr of EBITDA and is not in any scenario
Net debt is taken at the June seasonal low in cash (JPY190.9bn) rather than the March figure (JPY136.9bn), a ~JPY200/share difference the reader should be aware of
Terminal cap at 14x owner FCF binds in the base case; at 6% WACC the Gordon value would be materially higher
JFTC outcome for Haseko Reform is unquantified beyond the bear narrative
